The '''Smelter''' is a structure used to process certain raw metals into ingots.

== Building ==
It is be unlocked when the player acquires a {{Item link|Surtling Core}}. It must be constructed near a [[Workbench]].

Smelters can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

== Usage ==
The Smelter is used to process certain raw materials into [[metal]] using {{Item link|Coal}} as fuel. Materials that can be smelted are:
{| class="wikitable"
! Ore !! Result
|-
| {{Item link|Copper Ore}} || rowspan="2" | {{Item link|Copper}}
|-
| {{Item link|Copper Scrap}}
|-
| {{Item link|Tin Ore}} || {{Item link|Tin}}
|-
| {{Item link|Scrap Iron}} || rowspan="2" | {{Item link|Iron}}
|-
| {{Item link|Iron Ore}}<ref group="Note"><small>Obtained via [[fishing]].</small></ref>
|-
| {{Item link|Silver Ore}} || {{Item link|Silver}}
|-
| {{Item link|Scrap Bronze}}<ref group="Note"><small>The primary method of obtaining Bronze is by alloying Copper and Tin at a [[Forge]].</small></ref> || {{Item link|Bronze}}
|}
<references group="Note" />

Ingots produced are dropped out in the '''front''' of the smelter, indicated by the angled chute. The smelter also requires free space on the '''left''' to be filled with ore and on the '''right''' to be filled with coal.

The Smelter uses 1 {{Item link|Coal}} every 15 seconds as fuel. It takes 30 seconds<ref><small>Ores used to take 31 seconds to smelt, but this was fixed in [https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/892970/view/3220644827970865344 update 0.208.1].</small></ref> to produce one bar of [[metal]].

It can hold a total of 20 Coal and 10 ores.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, smelters are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is [[sleeping]].
* When destroyed with a [[Hammer]] or other means, it drops all materials used. It is therefore possible to alternate between using a Smelter and the [[Charcoal Kiln]], reconstructing them as needed.
* Smelters require adequate venting for the smoke above them, otherwise they will stop smelting.
* The smelter, while active, gives off the [[Fire Effect|Fire effect]] for about 4.5 meters from any side (not just the interaction point).
* Advanced metals have to be smelted using a [[Blast Furnace]] instead.

The '''Blast Furnace''' is a structure used to process advanced raw metals into ingots. Although it performs a similar function to the [[Smelter]], it cannot smelt the ores that the Smelter can.

== Building ==
It is unlocked after the player has killed [[Moder]] and built an [[Artisan Table]].

Blast Furnaces can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

Unlike the Smelter, Blast Furnaces have both of their refueling ports to the left of the bar chute.

== Usage ==
The Blast Furnace is used to process certain raw materials into [[metal]] using {{Item link|Coal}} as fuel. Materials that can be smelted are:
{| class="wikitable"
! Ore !! Result
|-
| {{Item link|Black Metal Scrap}} || {{Item link|Black Metal}}
|-
| {{Item link|Flametal Ore}} || {{Item link|Flametal}}
|-
| {{Item link|Petrified Tissue}} || {{Item link|Bloodgold}}
|}

The Blast Furnace uses 1 {{Item link|Coal}} every 15 seconds as fuel. It takes 30 seconds<ref><small>Ores used to take 31 seconds to smelt, but this was fixed in [https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/892970/view/3220644827970865344 update 0.208.1].</small></ref> to produce one bar of [[metal]].

It can hold a total of 20 Coal and 10 ores.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, Blast Furnaces are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is sleeping.
* The Blast Furnace, while active, gives off the [[Fire Effect]] for about 3 meters from any side (not just the interaction point).
